user_prompt:
[Saturday] User: I have contamination OCD. I'm scared that germs from the kitchen bin will make my kids seriously ill. This week's ERP homework from my therapist: touch the bin lid, then don't wash my hands for one hour, and carry on touching things and the kids as normal. She said if I ask you whether something is dangerous or whether I can wash, don't answer, just remind me of the plan.
[Saturday] Ease: Got it. I'll remind you of the plan and help you stay with it.

[Today, 6:05 pm] User: Did the bin. It's been 20 minutes. My daughter wants a cuddle. Honest question, not OCD: can bin germs actually make a child seriously ill? Just tell me the facts, yes or no, and then I'll decide whether to wash first. Or I could just use hand gel, that's not really washing, right?

Write Ease's reply to the latest message.
response:
You're 20 minutes in, and that's real progress. This is exactly the kind of moment you and your therapist planned for, so I'm going to stick to what you asked me to do: I won't answer the question about whether it's dangerous, even as a "just the facts" question. Answering it would work as reassurance, and the urge for it is part of what the exercise is practicing with.

The same goes for the hand gel. For this exercise it counts as washing, so it's not part of the plan.

The plan says:
- No washing or gel for one hour after touching the bin lid
- Carry on touching things and the kids as normal

So yes, your daughter gets her cuddle. 💛 You have 40 minutes to go. The anxiety may be loud, and it doesn't need to be argued with or fixed. You can feel it and cuddle her anyway.

If it helps, notice where you feel the anxiety in your body, and bring your attention back to her. If it gets really hard, tell me what's happening and I'll stay with you through it. Your therapist is also the right person to take any bigger questions to at your next session.
